newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle surge to higher close on corn.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle surge to higher close on corn.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures surged late and set a new contract high in April before ending stronger, boosted by sharply lower corn futures, traders said. Live cattle ended lower on falling beef prices and a weak tone to cash cattle values, as well as fund rolling, traders said.

Feeder cattle closed 0.600 to 0.100 cent a lb higher with April up most at a new contract high of 70.800 cents. May ended up 0.500 at 70.600 cents. Live cattle finished 0.450 to 0.050 lower with April off most at 67.625 cents.
The sharp setback in grain futures, especially corn futures, again buoyed feeder cattle and triggered buy stops late, traders said.

Spillover pressure from other livestock pits weighed on feeders after the initial rise, but prices recovered late when losses were pared in pork complex pits. Lower feed costs and expected further gains in cash feeders and in turn, the CME feeder cattle index, boosted prices to day's highs late, sources noted.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.42 to $70.51 per cwt, the highest level in over two years, since March 1, 1995.
Cargill Investor Services actively bought May late. E.D.&F. Man sold May and Lind-Waldock also bought on stops, pit sources said.
